newsitem.title: USA: Teltrend falls after Q1 earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: Teltrend falls after Q1 earnings warning.

text.p: Shares of Teltrend Inc fell nearly 21 percent on Wednesday after the company warned it expects to report fiscal 1997 first quarter earnings at the low end of estimates and that it sees continued weakness in orders.

"I think the stock is down over fears of continued weakness in the second quarter," said Greg Mesniaeff, telecom equipment analyst for Robinson-Humphrey Co, adding he cut his fiscal 1997 earnings estimate to $2.11 a share from $2.18.
Teltrend said Tuesday it will likely post earnings for its fiscal first quarter of $0.48 a share versus $0.47 last year. The First Call consensus of estimates was $0.51 a share.

Teltrend, a manufacturer of advanced telephone loop products based in St. Charles, Ill., said inventory consolidations at two of its major regional Bell operating companies customers cut into earnings.
The company said it expects the consolidation efforts to continue somewhat during November and December, "and then the buying of these two customers will return to normal."
"I think there is an overreaction here," said Michael Neiberg, an analyst with Furman Selz.

Teltrend said it did expect to report a rise in earnings and revenues, that fiscal second quarter earnings will be ahead of the first, and the second half will be considerably stronger than the first half.
"It's important that they do say that they are going to see sequential growth," Neiberg said, noting that the upcoming second quarter is historically weak for the company.
